James A. Whitman  
555 Oak Street, Springfield, IL 62704  
james.whitman@email.com | 555-123-4567  

Professional Summary  
Results-driven finance analyst with over 7 years of experience in financial analysis and technical leadership. A dedicated team player who has been responsible for mentoring junior staff and supporting financial operations. Seeking to contribute analytical skills and collaborative mindset in a dynamic finance environment.

Work Experience  

Senior Finance Analyst  
Linton Financial Services, Chicago, IL  
March 2018 - August 2023  
- Was responsible for preparing financial reports and statements  
- Duties included analyzing budget data and forecasting trends  
- Assisted in coordinating with different departments on financial matters  
- Managed project deliverables related to finance processes  
- Provided mentorship to team members and new hires  
- Participated in meetings to discuss financial strategies and plans  

Finance Analyst  
Hartley & Co., Springfield, IL  
January 2015 - February 2018  
- Was responsible for compiling and reviewing financial data  
- Duties included supporting budgeting and forecasting activities  
- Assisted in maintaining accurate financial records  
- Participated in team efforts for process improvements  
- Provided support for month-end and year-end closing activities  
- Collaborated with other departments as part of project teams  

Junior Finance Analyst  
Beckman Group, Springfield, IL  
July 2012 - December 2014  
- Was responsible for data collection and entry for financial reports  
- Duties included preparing basic financial summaries and analyses  
- Assisted in developing financial documentation  
- Supported senior analysts in various tasks  
- Attended training sessions on financial tools and processes  
- Provided general administrative support to finance team  

Finance Intern  
Davis & Partners, Springfield, IL  
May 2011 - August 2011  
- Supported the finance team with daily administrative tasks  
- Assisted in data gathering for financial reports  
- Was responsible for organizing financial documents  
- Participated in team meetings and took notes  
- Helped with preparation of presentations  
- Learned about financial analysis processes and software  

Education  

Bachelor of Science in Finance  
State University, Springfield, IL  
Graduated May 2012  

Skills  
- Financial reporting and analysis  
- Budgeting and forecasting support  
- Team collaboration and mentorship  
- MS Excel and financial software usage  
- Basic project coordination  
- Strong communication and organizational skills

Edit

Managed project deliverables related to finance processes; [verified detail].

OTHER LINE REWRITES

Useful edits, kept with their own source.

These do not map uniquely to the ranked fixes above, so each stays beside the exact line it rewrites.

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“- Was responsible for preparing financial reports and statements”

REWRITE

Prepared financial reports and statements for [stakeholder group], covering [reporting scope]; [measurable result]

Add the reporting audience, scale, and result so the work reads beyond routine preparation.

LINE EDIT 02 · SOURCE LINE

“- Duties included analyzing budget data and forecasting trends”

REWRITE

Analyzed budget data and forecast trends across [budget scope], providing [analysis or recommendation] to [stakeholder group]; [measurable result]

Add the budget size or coverage, the analysis delivered, and what changed after it was used.

LINE EDIT 03 · SOURCE LINE

“- Participated in team efforts for process improvements”

REWRITE

Participated in process-improvement work for [finance process], contributing [specific action]; [measurable result]

Add the process, your contribution, and the resulting change to distinguish participation from a general claim.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

Which finance process did you own at Linton, and where did your responsibility stop?

Why it may help: Your senior title sits beside several bullets using responsible, assisted, and participated, leaving ownership boundaries unclear.

QUESTION 02

How many departments, budgets, entities, or reports did you handle at Linton Financial Services?

Why it may help: The resume mentions financial reporting and cross-department coordination but gives no size indicator.

QUESTION 03

What changed when you supported month-end and year-end closing at Hartley & Co.?

Why it may help: Closing work is named, but the page does not show deadlines, accuracy demands, or the result of your contribution.

QUESTION 04

What process improvement did you participate in at Hartley & Co., and what changed afterward?

Why it may help: The improvement bullet needs the specific process and measurable or observable change.

QUESTION 05

Which departments did you coordinate with, and what finance issue did the collaboration resolve?

Why it may help: The resume mentions different departments without identifying the stakeholders or the problem addressed.

KEEP THESE

The parts already earning trust.
01

Your titles show a steady progression from Finance Intern in 2011 to Senior Finance Analyst in 2018, which makes the career direction immediately recognizable.

02

Financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, closing, and process work recur across multiple roles, giving the resume a coherent finance foundation.

03

The Linton role includes mentorship and project deliverables, useful details for showing responsibilities beyond individual analysis.

ROLE DIRECTION

Where this story reads strongest.

Position yourself around financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, and finance-process coordination. Replace general collaboration language with the reports, budgets, stakeholders, and results you can verify.

BEST FIT NOW

Senior Financial Analyst
Financial Planning and Analysis Analyst
Corporate Finance Analyst

Seniority read: The Senior Finance Analyst title and seven-plus years in finance support senior individual-contributor roles, but the bullets do not yet establish people-management or broad ownership.
